title: Book 4 — Melpomene, Chapter 23
paragraphs: As far as the country of these Scythians, the whole land described is level plain with deep soil. But after this point it is stony and rugged. When one has passed through a great extent of this rugged country, there dwell in the skirts of lofty mountains men who are said to be all bald-headed from their birth, male and female alike, with flat noses and large chins. They speak a language of their own, use the Scythian manner of dress, and live on the produce of trees. The tree whose fruit they live on is called the Pontic tree, and is about the size of a fig tree. It bears a fruit the size of a bean, containing a stone. When the fruit is ripe, they strain it through cloths, and there flows from it a thick black juice, which is called aschy. This they either lick up or drink mixed with milk, and from the lees—the solid part—they make cakes and use them for food; for they have few cattle, since the pastures there are not good. Each man has his dwelling under a tree, in winter covering the tree all round with close white felt cloth, and in summer leaving it uncovered. These people are injured by no one, for they are said to be sacred, and they possess no weapon of war. They are the ones who decide disputes among their neighbours; and besides this, any fugitive who takes refuge with them is injured by no one. They are called Argippaians.
